encounters.cc: Follow-up visit for prospective cohort study of antihypertensive medication

lines: Follow-up visit for prospective cohort study of antihypertensive medication
This 55-year-old male with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus returns for follow-up care following his routine check-up in January 2020 for ongoing hyperlipidemia management.
He is enrolled in a prospective cohort study assessing the relationship between a new antihypertensive medication and the incidence of myocardial infarction (MI) among high-risk patients.
He reports compliance with the medication regimen and has no new complaints.
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
He has no chest pain, dyspnea, or edema.
His blood pressure today is 132/84 mmHg.
His previous cholesterol levels were LDL 160 mg/dL and HDL 40 mg/dL.
The study coordinator informs you that 20% of the study participants have been lost to follow-up.
He is scheduled for a follow-up lipid panel next month.

lines: Routine health maintenance visit with concerns regarding lung cancer risk

- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy

lines: Progressive exertional dyspnea and nonproductive cough over 6 months
The patient with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents following prior cardiology evaluation for exertional chest pressure and previous pulmonary risk assessment.
He denies any recent travel or sick contacts.
- Isolated pharmacologic pain management without immobilization (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
His family history is significant for coronary artery disease in his father.
He has a 30-pack-year smoking history and works in construction.
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air.
Lung auscultation reveals bilateral end-inspiratory crackles.
Chest X-ray shows diffuse interstitial infiltrates.
High-resolution CT scan of the chest demonstrates subpleural reticular changes and honeycombing without significant lymphadenopathy.
Pulmonary function tests show a restrictive pattern with reduced diffusion capacity.
